items.text: Decision (2026-11-03): the YAML storage, to sit next to JSONStorage so ops can hand-edit tinydb files, was planned to use PyYAML with a SafeLoader subclass in which only true/false load as booleans; `NO`, `off`, `yes`, `on` stay strings, with the dumper keeping stock resolvers so strings like "NO" are written quoted. Plain `yaml.safe_load` was rejected (YAML 1.1 turns `country: NO` and `maintenance: off` into booleans) as was ruamel.yaml (unwanted extra dependency). Revised later on 2026-11-03: the YAML storage was implemented (no longer deferred), but it reads with plain `yaml.safe_load`, so the custom boolean-restricting SafeLoader from this decision is not what was implemented.

In tinydb/storages.py, file handling (touch/create_dirs, access-mode warning, opening `self._handle`, `close()`) was refactored on 2026-11-03 into a new abstract base class `FileStorage(path, create_dirs, encoding, access_mode)`, exported in `__all__`. `JSONStorage` now inherits from it and keeps `**kwargs`, `read()` and `write()`. All 228 tests passed (run with `-o addopts=""` because pytest.ini's `--cov` flags are unavailable). The change was uncommitted. It was a reusable base for YAMLStorage, which later the same day was added as a second subclass of `FileStorage`.

Planned design for the later YAMLStorage: built on FileStorage; parse errors must raise instead of returning None (TinyDB treats None as an empty DB, risking wiping the file, as the docs example with YAMLError does); document ID keys normalized to str on read; comments in the file are lost on rewrite with PyYAML. Open questions: core module vs extension package, and whether losing comments is acceptable to ops.

Table.update and Table.remove now skip missing doc_ids instead of raising KeyError (May 2026, #616, fixes #591). IDs are filtered inside the updater so operations are atomic, avoiding half-applied in-place updates from shared references; upsert dropped its except KeyError branch. This made get/update/remove consistent.

Query handling and cacheability: v4.6.0 (Dec 2021–Jan 2022) added a `map` query operation (#445) with callables marked noncacheable, and required `is_cacheable` on every query, which broke plain callables. v4.6.1 (2022-01-18) revised this: `is_cacheable` is only called if present on the query object, otherwise the query is treated as cacheable (Fixes #454). Docs note backwards-compatibility concerns when adding query methods.

TinyDB v4.0 (released 2020-05-02, work from Nov 2019, rationale in #284, closing #250 and #103; led by Markus Siemens) was a major architectural refactor to simplify the architecture, drop legacy support and enable extension via subclassing: Python 2 support, deprecated `ujson` support and the deprecated element ID API were removed, project configuration moved to Poetry, type annotations were added, and subclassing helpers (Extension Mechanisms) were introduced. Upgrade notes and a changelog accompanied the release.
YAML support work in tinydb: YAML tests were made to run as part of the test suite and PyYAML was added to setup.py.

October 2026 bug-fix wave on Query/Table correctness (Utkarsh Adhran, 2026-10-06): Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes as sequences (uses collections.abc.Sequence, #641, fixes #638); regex flags are now part of the matches/search query hash so case-insensitive and case-sensitive searches no longer share a cache entry (#640, fixes #637); persist_empty no longer wipes existing table data on reopen (#642, fixes #636).

TinyDB underwent a major architectural refactor for v4.0 (rationale and details in #284, closing #250 and #103): dropped Python 2 support, removed deprecated `ujson` support and the deprecated element ID API, switched to Poetry for project configuration, added type annotations, and added subclassing helpers (Extension Mechanisms in #284).
